title: Legal Research and Case Strategy
answer: Retrieval-grounded research, adversarial statutory reading, brief drafting, citation auditing and jurisdictional anomalies.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Retrieval-Grounded Legal Research
children.blurb: Retrieval-grounded legal research covers the use of AI systems that answer legal questions by first retrieving relevant passages from primary and secondary sources, then generating a response tied to those passages.

children.name: Adversarial Statutory Interpretation
children.blurb: Adversarial statutory interpretation is the practice of using computational tools to identify competing readings of a statute, test how courts might resolve ambiguity, and map the interpretive moves available to each side in litigation.

children.name: Brief Drafting with Machine Assistance
children.blurb: Brief drafting with machine assistance covers the use of AI tools to help lawyers prepare motions, briefs, memoranda, and other court filings.

children.name: Citation Auditing and Good Law Checking
children.blurb: Citation auditing and good law checking is the process of verifying that every authority cited in a legal document remains valid, has not been overruled or reversed, and still supports the proposition for which it is cited.

children.name: Jurisdictional Anomalies and Local Codes
children.blurb: This page covers the uneven patchwork of state, county, and municipal rules that apply to artificial intelligence, where definitions, enforcement dates, and obligations differ from one locality to the next.

sections.body: This field is about using AI systems to find law, read statutes, draft briefs, check citations, and track local rules. In practice, current tools retrieve passages from case law and statutes, summarize them, and propose arguments, but they do not replace a lawyer's judgment. Retrieval grounded research ties answers to sources so a person can inspect the cited authority. Adversarial statutory interpretation uses models to generate competing readings of a text and to surface ambiguities. Brief drafting with machine assistance helps assemble facts, authorities, and standard sections, while citation auditing checks whether a case is still good law. Jurisdictional anomalies and local codes matter because a rule in one court may not hold in another.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Retrieval and citation checking are useful but still fail on opaque sources, sealed documents, and outdated databases. Fabricated citations remain a known failure mode, so verification remains essential. The site tracks 29 AI case law precedents, which shows that appellate guidance is still thin and mostly recent. There are 146 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, and those disputes shape how research tools may use protected material. Statutory reading by machine can produce plausible but wrong interpretations, especially when a term is defined elsewhere or a local rule overrides a general one, so the honest limit is that AI can accelerate search and drafting but cannot certify that a filing is correct or that a strategy is sound.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages fit together as a workflow. Retrieval-Grounded Legal Research is the entry point for finding authority with traceable sources. Adversarial Statutory Interpretation takes a statute or rule and tests rival readings before a brief commits to one. Brief Drafting with Machine Assistance covers how to assemble a document while keeping human review in the loop. Citation Auditing and Good Law Checking is the safety step, where each authority is verified against current law, and Jurisdictional Anomalies and Local Codes is the final check for courts, counties, and agencies that depart from the general rule. A reader would go to the first for source gathering, the second for argument testing, the third for drafting, the fourth for verification, and the fifth for local variation.
